title: A pope under siege
text: The oldest letters on this map run from Avignon to Barcelona, in the years when two rival popes claimed the Church.
Benedict XIII, besieged in Avignon, writes in cipher to his agent Francesc Climent about the embassy of Aragon, Castile and Navarre, the submission he refused, and a demand for 3,000 francs.

title: A duke begs his son-in-law
text: In the last months of his life Filippo Maria Visconti, Duke of Milan, writes again and again to Francesco Sforza, the captain who had married his daughter and whom he had fought.

After the rout of his army he drops his grudge and begs Sforza to come. He even asks Sforza to plant a trusted man at his own court, posing as a deserter. From Rome, envoys report a dead pope, a conclave and what King Alfonso will pay.

title: Hungary and the War of Ferrara
text: Venice opens a war on Ferrara in 1482, and the routes swing to Hungary.

Queen Beatrice tells her sister, the Duchess of Ferrara, that for 100,000 ducats King Matthias would raise 16,000 men against Venice. The Ferrarese envoy learns in great secrecy that Venice is bidding for the same king.

title: Rome in the Italian Wars
text: Clement VII is caught between Charles V and Francis I, and every court wants to know what he will do next.

After the Colonna raid on the Vatican in 1526 he sighs to the French agent that he has thought of fleeing Rome. In December 1527 the Marquis del Vasto tells Charles V how he means to march the army out of the city, and that it cannot be kept without money. In London in 1529, du Bellay goes to see Wolsey after his fall.

title: The Armada years
text: The lines to London thicken as England and Spain move towards war, and France tears itself apart.

In Paris, Sir Edward Stafford's cipher runs name the plan to kill the King of Navarre. At Ostend in March 1588, Lord Cobham warns that the garrison is short of money and that Parma's new ditch to Sluys is nearly navigable for his boats. In August 1589 a letter from Rome carries the news that Henri III has been killed.

title: A nuncio at the Emperor's court
text: One route takes over the map around 1629: Vienna to Rome, in the middle of the Thirty Years' War.

The nuncio Giovanni Battista Pallotta reports on the Emperor's ministers, the dispute over Mantua and the Edict of Restitution. He also watches Wallenstein, who has gout and is holding back from Italy.

title: Across the Atlantic
text: Here the map has to widen. In August 1760 the Governor of New France reports from Montréal on the eve of the capitulation: no powder, no food, and the British closing in.
A year later Martinique is ordering flour and beef for a siege. By 1801 the secrets run to Washington, with word from Paris that Spain has ceded Louisiana to France.

title: Telegrams to and from Tokyo
text: Chinese revolutionaries in exile work the telegraph from Japan. Sun Yat-sen wires Soong Ching-ling in Shanghai, and even the love telegrams go into cipher.

The Japanese Foreign Ministry intercepts a telegram from Swatow to Sun's household and cannot read it. It reports that Sun's men recovered Swatow, and that Mo Qingyu then arrived with a large force and ordered them out.

title: The last arcs
text: In January 1917 Bernstorff warns Berlin from Washington that its memorandum on armed merchant ships could bring a break with the United States. In 1921 Moscow is wiring gold rubles to Berlin to pay for its orders.
The last arcs on the map are police radio. In June 1942 a message from Mogilev tells Himmler that the village of Borki was razed and its inhabitants killed. It survives in Bletchley Park's decrypt.
